subject: English
topic: One-Word Substitution in Context — SSC CGL Tested Vocabulary (W12 B1)

questions.stem: A person who has a strong hatred of and contempt for the human race is called a ___.
questions.explanation: C is correct. MISANTHROPE = a person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general (from Greek misein = hate + anthropos = human being). Famous literary misanthropes: Ebenezer Scrooge, Sherlock Holmes (somewhat). Trap: misogynist = hatred specifically of women (miso + gyne); philanthropist = lover of humanity (the opposite of misanthrope); pessimist = one who expects the worst (not the same as hating people).

questions.stem: The psychiatrist noted the patient's intense and irrational fear of water. This condition is known as ___.
questions.explanation: B is correct. HYDROPHOBIA = morbid fear of water (Greek hydro = water + phobia = fear). Also a symptom of rabies in advanced stages. Trap: acrophobia = fear of heights (acro = heights); claustrophobia = fear of confined spaces (claustro = enclosed); agoraphobia = fear of open or crowded spaces (agora = marketplace/open area). Memory tip: HYDRO = water (hydraulic, hydrant, dehydration).

questions.stem: A system of government in which the supreme power lies with the people, exercised directly or through elected representatives, is called ___.
questions.explanation: D is correct. DEMOCRACY = government by the people (Greek demos = people + kratos = rule/power). Lincoln: 'government of the people, by the people, for the people.' Trap: oligarchy = rule by a small group of powerful people; theocracy = rule by religious authority or God's law; autocracy = rule by one person with absolute power (auto = self). All end in '-cracy' (rule) but have different prefix meanings.

questions.stem: The zoo's new facility, where birds of various species live in a large enclosed space, is called an ___.
questions.explanation: B is correct. AVIARY = a large enclosure for keeping birds in captivity (Latin avis = bird). Trap: apiary = a place where bees are kept (Latin apis = bee); aquarium = where fish/aquatic animals are kept (Latin aqua = water); herbarium = a collection of dried, pressed plants (Latin herba = plant/grass). Key root: AVI = bird (aviation, aviator — both involve flying, like birds).

questions.stem: The doctor found the patient walking around the hospital corridors with eyes open but completely unconscious, a condition called ___.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SOMNAMBULISM = the condition of walking and sometimes performing other actions while asleep; sleepwalking (Latin somnus = sleep + ambulare = to walk). Trap: insomnia = inability to sleep (Latin in- = not + somnus = sleep); hypnosis = induced sleep-like trance (for suggestion); narcolepsy = uncontrollable attacks of deep sleep during the day. Mnemonic: SOMN = sleep (somnolent = drowsy), AMBLE = walk (ambulance = vehicle that carries).

questions.stem: His grandfather collected ancient Roman coins and medals, a hobby known as ___.
questions.explanation: B is correct. NUMISMATICS = the study or collection of coins, paper money, and medals (Latin numisma = coin, from Greek nomisma = current coin). Trap: philately = the collection and study of postage stamps (Greek philos = loving + ateleia = tax-free, referring to prepaid postage); cartophily = collection of cigarette cards; 'numismatology' = not a real standard English word (numismatics is the accepted term). SSC PYQ favourite: philately (stamps) vs numismatics (coins).

questions.stem: The manager suspected that the employee was pretending to be sick to avoid a difficult assignment — a behaviour described as ___.
questions.explanation: A is correct. MALINGERING = deliberately feigning or exaggerating illness or incapacity to avoid duty or work, especially in a military or employment context (origin uncertain, possibly from French malingre = weakly sickly). One who does it: a malingerer. Trap: hypochondria = genuinely believing oneself to be ill when one is not (the hypochondriac is sincere, not faking); feigning = pretending in general (a verb, not a noun label for the specific behaviour); shirking = avoiding work but not specifically by faking illness — the one-word substitution that most precisely fits is malingering.

questions.stem: The minister delivered a brilliant speech on education policy without any notes or prior preparation. Such a speech is described as ___.
questions.explanation: C is correct. IMPROMPTU = done without being planned or rehearsed; on the spur of the moment (Latin in promptu = in readiness, but used to mean without preparation). Also: extempore = spoken without preparation (from the same idea). Trap: verbose = using more words than necessary (the opposite quality from what's described — the speech was brilliant); eloquent = fluent and persuasive speaking (quality of delivery, not preparation status); rehearsed = the opposite of impromptu.

questions.stem: Despite every setback, she always believed things would turn out well. Her friends called her an incurable ___.
questions.explanation: A is correct. OPTIMIST = a person who tends to take a hopeful or positive view of future outcomes (from Latin optimus = best). Antonym: pessimist (expects the worst). Trap: realist = one who accepts situations as they actually are (neither optimistic nor pessimistic); altruist = one who selflessly considers others' welfare before their own (about actions, not worldview); narcissist = one who is excessively self-admiring (personality trait, not related to outlook on events).

questions.stem: Professor Mehta is an authority on the study and collection of national flags of various countries. His area of expertise is called ___.
questions.explanation: D is correct. VEXILLOLOGY = the study of flags, their history, symbolism and usage (from Latin vexillum = small sail/flag + Greek -logia = study). Coined in 1959 by Whitney Smith. Trap: heraldry = the study of coats of arms and armorial bearings (shields, family crests — not flags per se); cartography = making and studying maps (Latin charta = paper/map); numismatics = study of coins and medals (Q6). SSC occasionally tests rare -ology words: vexillology (flags), seismology (earthquakes), ornithology (birds), entomology (insects).
